title: CHAR Data Type
description: Learn how to use the CHAR data type to store fixed-length, non-Unicode character strings.

data.text: The CHAR data type stores fixed-length, non-Unicode character strings. Use CHAR when the sizes of values in the column are fixed.

data.title: CHAR Syntax
data.content: Defines a CHAR column with a specified length.

data.text: n specifies the string length from 1 to 8,000. If not specified, the default value is 1.

data.title: Create CHAR Column
data.content: Creates a table with a CHAR(3) column.

data.text: When you insert a string shorter than the defined length, SQL Server adds trailing spaces. When you select the value, SQL Server removes the trailing spaces.

data.title: Insert and Query CHAR Value
data.content: Inserts a 3-character string and queries it.
data.code:
INSERT INTO test.sql_server_char (val)
VALUES ('ABC');

SELECT
    val,
    LEN(val) len,
    DATALENGTH(val) data_length
FROM
    sql_server_char;

data.text: Even though the character 'A' is only one character, the number of bytes is fixed at three. LEN returns the number of characters excluding trailing blanks, while DATALENGTH returns the number of bytes.

items: CHAR is fixed-length; VARCHAR is variable-length.
CHAR pads values with trailing spaces; VARCHAR does not.
Use CHAR when data sizes are consistent; use VARCHAR when sizes vary.

data.text: CHAR values are padded on the right, and SQL Server follows the ANSI setting `SET ANSI_PADDING` for how the padding is stored. By default, trailing spaces are ignored for comparison, so `'A1'` and `'A1  '` are equal in a WHERE clause. The script below proves it and shows how to see the stored bytes.

data.title: Padding in practice
data.content: LEN ignores trailing spaces; DATALENGTH counts the stored bytes.

data.title: Common mistake
data.text: Do not reach for CHAR just because a value "looks fixed". It is the right choice for values such as ISO currency codes (`CHAR(3)`) or state codes, but for anything that varies it wastes space and makes string concatenation surprising. Also remember that a CHAR column compared to a VARCHAR parameter can cause an implicit conversion that blocks index seeks.

data.title: CHAR Key Points
points: CHAR stores fixed-length, non-Unicode character strings.
Trailing spaces are added for shorter values and removed on select.
Use CHAR when data sizes are consistent across rows.
